# Bare `npx playwright test` reports zero tests and a stack trace, and nothing warns a human

## Context

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now documents the engine's test tiers (#18999), and an external contributor landed three artifacts tonight (PR #19015, #19016, PR #19017). @tobiu's correction to @neo-opus-grace on that review names what a newcomer needs beyond a verdict — *"giving some hints and input on the neo ecosystem"* — and item one on her list is **which test tier a change belongs in and that bare `npx playwright test` silently selects the wrong set**.

Two agent skills already carry it as a CRITICAL warning (`ticket-create`, `pull-request`: *"Do NOT run default `npx playwright test`"*). **Nothing tells a human.**

## The Problem

> **⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-20T00:50Z — this section originally described the wrong command's output.** @neo-gpt-emmy's RA-1 on PR #19019 caught it: I measured with `npx playwright test --list` and attributed its `Total: 0 tests in 0 files` summary — a `ListModeReporter` line — to the bare run. **This ticket's own Avoided Traps said "do not quote the error from this ticket, re-run it on the branch"; I re-ran it with a flag the prose did not name.** The re-measurement below is the bare command itself, and the true behaviour is a better explanation than the one it replaces.

Measured on this branch at 2026-09-20T00:48Z, bare `npx playwright test` — no `-c`, no `--list`:

```
Error fetching SEO metadata: [TypeError: Failed to parse URL from undefinedapps/portal/resources/data/seo.json]
…
Error: The neuralLink fixture requires NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT to name an absolute
neo-agent-brain checkout; Engine cwd fallback is forbidden.
   at test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:51
   at test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPerspectivesNL.spec.mjs:3:40
exit=1
```

92 lines: **1** `Error fetching SEO metadata`, **12** `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, and **no test-result line of any kind**. It does not report zero tests — without a config it collects *every* tier's specs at once, under *no* tier's environment, and dies during collection. There is no `playwright.config.*` at the repository root; the eight configs live in `test/playwright/`, and the npm scripts target them explicitly.

The failure mode is the problem, not the missing config. A newcomer running the command their Playwright experience predicts gets **an apparently broken repository**, not a wrong-command message. Same class as the `dist/` gap #18999 already documents — an infrastructure error where a test result belongs — and it reads the same way: this project does not work.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/playwright.config.{mjs,unit,unit-tz,component,e2e,matrix,visual,update-chain}.mjs` — eight configs, none at root.
- `package.json` scripts `test`, `test-unit`, `test-unit-tz`, `test-components`, `test-e2e` each pass `-c` explicitly.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` §*Set up the engine from a clone* already teaches the tiers and already explains one looks-broken-but-is-not trap. This is its sibling and belongs beside it.

## The Fix

Four or five lines in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, next to the existing test block: name the trap, show what it prints, and point at the `npm run test-*` scripts as the only supported entry points. No code change, no new config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC-1** — `CONTRIBUTING.md` states that bare `npx playwright test` is not a supported entry point, and that the `npm run test-*` scripts are.
- [x] **AC-2** — it names the **observable**, attributed to the command that produces it: the bare run exits 1 having run no test, after a stack trace about SEO metadata and repeated `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` fixture errors — so a reader who already hit it recognises their own symptom rather than only being warned in advance.
- [x] **AC-3** — the claim is re-measured on the branch **with the exact command the prose names**, and the quoted output matches what that command prints. A receipt for a differently-flagged invocation does not satisfy this.

## Out of Scope

- Adding a root `playwright.config.mjs`. A root config would make the bare command "work" by silently selecting some tier, which is a worse failure than refusing — and the choice of which tier is exactly what the contributor needs to make consciously.
- Changing any config or npm script.
- The agent-facing skill warnings; they already exist and are correct for their audience.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not fix this by making the bare command work.** The tiers differ in environment, not just selection; a default that quietly picks one teaches the wrong model.
- ⛔ **Do not quote the error from this ticket.** Re-run it on the branch — the stack trace names specs that move.
- ⛔ **Re-run the command the prose names, not a convenient neighbour of it.** `--list`, `--reporter=`, `--project=` and `-c` each change what Playwright prints. This trap was added *because* the first attempt fell into the one above it and still got the output wrong.
